delivery.code: the public GitHub repository https://github.com/Exiam6/wuji-floating-release (anyone can clone it; it holds no assets)
delivery.assets: tarballs, one per part (plain tar, no compression: a gzip sample of the large files saved only 7 % to 21 %), in a drive folder that the project shares (the assets do not go through GitHub): the folder `full` holds all of them with SHA256SUMS, ASSET_TERMS.txt and README.txt, and a sibling folder `rollout_only` repeats the manifest files of the CPU-only subset (its four tarballs are the same files as in `full`)
delivery.mano: not delivered: every user registers at https://mano.is.tue.mpg.de, downloads the MANO models (version 1.2) and puts MANO_RIGHT.pkl at mano/models/MANO_RIGHT.pkl in the asset root; `wf.py assets verify --parts mano` checks its sha256 and says what is missing

delivery.unpacked: all tarballs unpack into one folder, the asset bundle (wuji_floating_assets_<date>/ in our own build); its delivered files are listed in asset_manifests/SHA256SUMS.all
delivery.returns: for an issued batch: one archive (tar of the folder `wf.py pack-results` prepares) uploaded to returns/<name>/<date>/ in the drive folder shared with you for returns, with its sha256 sent to the project

sets.rollout_only: core, hands, batches, licences, a subset of the same files (download only these four tarballs and SHA256SUMS from `full`, then `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS`); it runs the CPU rollouts (robot-hand protocols included) once the MANO file is in place, and holds no model weights
sets.full: every part but mano and hug1 (both obtained by the user); it also runs the GPU jobs (HUG2, the 50k fine-tune, DINOv2, the pictures and the DSRL training sets; HUG1 after `wf.py assets fetch-hug1`)
